subject.title: [RFC] Multi-Session Architecture: Shared LLM + Isolated Sessions + Public Knowledge Base

question: Should this broad multi-session RFC remain the umbrella architecture tracker, or should maintainers supersede it with narrower product-approved session-family, routing, UI, and memory/security issues?
rationale: The request changes core routing, storage, UI, config, plugin assumptions, and shared-memory privacy policy, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent architecture or migration/security boundary.

options.title: Keep Umbrella And Split Work
options.body: Keep this issue open for high-level architecture coordination while moving approved slices into narrowly reviewable implementation trackers.

options.title: Supersede With Narrow Canonicals
options.body: Close this umbrella after designating active narrower issues, such as the topic-session family tracker, as the remaining canonical work.

options.title: Reject Broad Core Architecture
options.body: Close the RFC as too broad for core and require optional pieces to prove missing plugin/API seams before returning to OpenClaw core.

recommendation.title: Keep Umbrella And Split Work
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for high-level architecture coordination while moving approved slices into narrowly reviewable implementation trackers.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses core architecture, security posture, and session/routing surfaces where local history and maintainer policy point to steipete as the best available owner.
